notIdeasOfWhatSocietyShouldBe.explanation: Welfare spending is a type of government support (social security and social assistance programs), described by the article as a policy instrument, not a doctrine; the article records only that classical liberals, libertarians and conservatives criticize it while social democrats and socialists defend it, so it holds no positions of its own. I went through the statements (universal healthcare, tax the wealthy, basic income, equal outcomes, markets, minimum wage and the rest) and the article's sections on history, definitions, reform and national systems, and found no stated position of its own to answer on any of them, so fewer than two can be answered.
